title: THE DIVIDING HATRED: CORNELIUS THE CENTURION

sense.text:
Here is where the dividing begins. “But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites”: Solomon fell in love with heathen women.

These are the very nations the Lord had warned about: “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods.” Yet “Solomon clave unto these in love.” He had “seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.” He went off exactly the way the Lord said he would.

“When Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.” Letting the heathen in, out of love and emotion, is what turned the king's heart.

“Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem”: he built a sanctuary to a pagan god for his heathen Moabite wife, and one “for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon” for his Ammonite wife. “And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.”

Those sanctuaries were not built out of his own pocket. He used the money of the people to fund the heathen worship of his wives, and that is the heavy yoke of taxes Israel later begged his son to lift.
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice” about this very matter.

“Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant”, “even he lifted up his hand against the king.” Jeroboam tried to take Solomon out, and the chapter explains why.

Jeroboam “was a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.” A wise, hard-working man, raised up by Solomon himself over Joseph's house.

The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found Jeroboam alone in the field, “caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces”, ripped it, “And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee.” Ten tribes out of the twelve would go to Jeroboam.

“But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake”: that is Benjamin, who stayed with Judah. The cause: “they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians”, the Canaanites, “Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon”.

The Lord would not take the whole kingdom in Solomon's days, for David's sake, “But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes. And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem”. That one tribe is Benjamin: Benjamin and Judah always together.
Jeroboam was promised to “be king over Israel”, and a sure house like David's, if he would hearken and keep the statutes. “And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.”

“Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam.” Jeroboam had plotted against Solomon, trying to rush the prophecy and take the kingdom for himself. So he “fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.”
Solomon reigned “over all Israel” forty years, “And Solomon slept with his fathers”, “and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.” Solomon's son Rehoboam took the throne when he died.

“And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.” Rehoboam received his coronation in Shechem; he was anointed king there.

Why is Shechem so important? Because it is where Abraham first built a place of worship to the Lord, and it lies in the land that became Ephraim's. Keep Shechem in mind, and Bethel, Ai, Shiloh, Ebal and Gerizim: they are all in Ephraim's land, and that is where the beef between Ephraim and Judah starts.

precepts.why:
“Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee: And I will make of thee a great nation”. “And in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed”: Israel scattered abroad among those families.

Abram departed out of Haran, and “they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came.” Abraham was from Ur of the Chaldees, beyond the river Euphrates, where his father died; he went up to Haran and came down into Canaan. From Ur to Haran to Canaan is what is called the fertile crescent.

“And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Sichem, unto the plain of Moreh.” Sichem and Shechem are the same place, the place where Rehoboam was made king. There “the Lord appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord”. That was the first place of worship Abraham built in the land.

Then he removed “unto a mountain on the east of Beth–el, and pitched his tent, having Beth–el on the west, and Hai on the east: and there he builded an altar unto the Lord, and called upon the name of the Lord.” Shechem and Bethel: remember them, because later these places of worship are turned to idols.

“Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine”, and “the famine shall consume the land”. The dream was doubled “because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.”

Joseph was raised up to prophesy the seven years of famine in Egypt and how to prepare for it. Joseph saved Israel from starvation all the way in Egypt, and Joseph is Ephraim's father. That is one more reason Ephraim felt entitled.

Abraham himself fled a famine in Canaan down into Egypt, the same way Jacob and his sons later ran to Egypt in the famine. The parallels.

Isaac charged Jacob, “Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan”, and Jacob obeyed and went to Padan–aram. Esau, rebellious, saw “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father” and went and married anyway: “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling: there are your light-skinned Arabs.

Jacob lay down at a certain place and dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, the angels of God ascending and descending, and the Lord said, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. All four corners: Jacob's seed found in every corner of the earth, prophesied before they were born. “And in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: Israel would be scattered among those families.

Jacob woke and said, “Surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not.” “This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.” A portal to paradise. He set up the stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” There he vowed the tithe: “I will surely give the tenth unto thee.”

Bethel sits right under Shechem, in the same area, and Jacob also built an altar there between Bethel and Ai. This land is important to remember: Shechem, Bethel, Ai.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua, of Ephraim, fighting for us to gain the land promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

“And taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones in the land that did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, the same thing David did later as king. Another landmark in Ephraim's favour.

Joshua valiant in the wars: the men of Ai saw “the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way”. Israel smote them “so that they let none of them remain or escape”, and “all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai.” The king of Ai “he hanged on a tree until eventide”.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, an altar of whole stones as Moses commanded. All Israel “stood on this side the ark and on that side”, “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded before, that they should bless the people of Israel.” Israel received the cursings and the blessings of the law on those two mountains, Ebal and Gerizim, and they too are in Ephraim's land.

“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” Keep Shiloh in mind too. From this chapter on, each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Bethel, Shechem, Tappuah, Mount Gerizim and Ebal: all the earliest places of worship. Abraham's altar, the mountains of the law, the tabernacle at Shiloh, all in Ephraim's allotment, with Jerusalem and Bethlehem down in Judah.

So Ephraim felt entitled: there are more of us than Judah, and we have the places of worship, the historical monuments and landmarks. The beef starts here. This is the buildup of the dividing hatred.

sense.text:
Rehoboam was an idiot. Israel came and said, if you remove the yoke your father put upon us, the taxes he laid on the people to pay for the heathen sanctuaries of his wives, we will serve you forever. He said give me three days.

The old men, the elders who stood with Solomon and with David, said do what they ask and they will serve you forever. His boys he grew up with said you're the king now, flex on them. And “the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him; And spake to them after the counsel of the young men”. He chose the youths over the wise counsel of his elders.

“My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” Flexing for no reason. This guy is crazy.

“For the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.” Remember the prophet who rent the garment in twelve pieces and gave Jeroboam ten. Jeroboam jumped the gun and failed and ran to Egypt; when Solomon died he came back, and the prophecy was fulfilled that he would rise to the throne over the northern part of Israel. Judah kept only their brother Benjamin, and Benjamin stayed with Judah.

“What portion have we in David?” In other words, to hell with Judah. “Neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse”: we are done with Judah; y'all do y'all's thing, we're going to do ours. “To your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David”: go deal with your own tribe, you're not our king no more.

Rehoboam still reigned over the children of Israel in the cities of Judah. Then he “sent Adoram, who was over the tribute”: he sent a tax collector over to the northern kingdom, because he is an idiot. “And all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died.” They killed Adoram in front of him, and Rehoboam “made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem”, because they were going to kill him too. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

Jeroboam came back out of Egypt when he heard Solomon had passed, and Israel “made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.” Jeroboam had been King Solomon's servant, wise and industrious.

Rehoboam rounded up Judah and Benjamin, “an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel”, to go and take care of Ephraim for being rebellious and disrespectful.

But the word of God came to Shemaiah: “Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me.” Leave them alone, go home. I caused this; you are split for a reason. Leave the northern kingdom alone, leave Ephraim alone.

Jeroboam said in his heart, if this people keep going up to sacrifice at Jerusalem, where Judah is, even though we are not under their kingship anymore, their heart will turn back to Rehoboam “and they shall kill me”.

So he “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Jerusalem is too far, stay right here in our area; these calves I made are your gods.

“And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.” On the map, Bethel and Dan up north: rather than go south to Jerusalem to worship, go further north to the idols. The hell with Judah, we got our own idols now. “And this thing became a sin”.
“And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.” He fired Levi. Levi got laid off: get out of here, we don't need you.

Jeroboam ordained a feast “in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah”, sacrificing in Bethel unto the calves he made, “even in the month which he had devised of his own heart”. He made up his own feast day and had us worshipping idols instead.

That was the northern kingdom's place of worship, Bethel and Dan. From now on they would serve the Lord and those idols at the same time, and that goes right to John 4. Gerizim, Shechem, Shiloh, Bethel: all in the northern kingdom's land.

precepts.why:
“Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding”. Rehoboam was simple; that is why he would not listen to the elders. Of all Solomon's sons the Lord raised up the dumbest to be king, so he could split them in half. It is all the Lord.

“Who turned away the people through his counsel. There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”. Jeroboam was no better: he was the cause of Ephraim's sin from the beginning till now.

Ephraim's kings: NGK, no good kings. Not a single good king. Kings for two days, five minutes, two weeks, killing each other left and right, constant death and backstabbing like the Godfather. There were righteous Israelites in the northern kingdom, but the kings over them were bad. And they cannot let Jeroboam's idols go, even tonight: Santeria, Brujeria, Shango, white Jesus, the Catholic Church, rosary beads, child-molesting pastors and preachers. Diddy church, baby oil and nuns.
“Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” Samuel anointed David king in Bethlehem, in Judah.

David inquired of the Lord, “Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.” “And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.” David was anointed again in Hebron, but over Judah: king of Judah in Hebron.

“Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.” The elders of Israel made a league with him in Hebron “and they anointed David king over Israel.” At this point he is king over all twelve.

“In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.” Both kingdoms. “Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Zion is the city of David.

Remember, Ephraim had all the landmarks: Shiloh, Bethel, Ai, Ebal and Gerizim, all the areas of worship. Yet David was anointed in Bethlehem and in Hebron and reigned in Jerusalem, all in Judah.

The beef was already there before the split. “Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away”? Judah answered, “Because the king is near of kin to us”: he's our tribe. “Have we eaten at all of the king’s cost? or hath he given us any gift?” Did he bribe us?

“We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye”: there's more of us than you. Why can't we anoint him over here? “And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.” Judah cursed Ephraim out. That anger, that enmity between the two, never ended.

Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and rightfully so: Joseph saved Israel from starvation in Egypt, Joshua brought us into the land and gave out the allotments, and Abraham's altar at Shechem was in Ephraim's land. A lot of rivalry. So when the people cried “What portion have we in David?”, this is where it came from.

He “divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents. Yet they tempted and provoked the most high God”, and “provoked him to anger with their high places, and moved him to jealousy with their graven images.”

“So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men; And delivered his strength into captivity”. The young men were killed, “Their priests fell by the sword; and their widows made no lamentation.”

“Moreover he refused the tabernacle of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim: But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” He did not choose Ephraim because Ephraim went off first into idolatry with Jeroboam. “And he built his sanctuary like high palaces”, castles, and “He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds”.

Asaph wrote this. Ephraim was set aside for his idolatry and Judah was chosen, and the beef continues even after this.

“But seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to Beer–sheba”. These places were built for worship by Jacob and Abraham, and Ephraim turned them into places of idolatry.

“For Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Beth–el shall come to nought”: Ephraim will go into captivity, and Bethel shall be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”, that is Ephraim.

“Behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.” A plumbline is a measuring tool: judgment. “I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel”. “And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”

“Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el”, one of those low-level priests raised up who was not Levi, told Jeroboam, “Amos hath conspired against thee”, “the land is not able to bear all his words.” Amos was preaching the word of God and they did not want to hear it: get this troublemaker out of here, same as Jacob today. Amos had prophesied, “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land”: Assyria overthrowing Ephraim.

“O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.” Go teach Judah, you bother us over here. That's how you know the northern kingdom. You're disturbing the king's church services: Amos was blitzing the churches back then.

Amos was no prophet nor a prophet's son, but a herdman, “and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. “Drop not thy word against the house of Isaac”: the house of Isaac is the northern kingdom, and it goes back to the Saxons.

“Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city”: they will rape your wives, enslave you and make your wives hoes. “Thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line”, taken and divided among them like it is to this day, “and thou shalt die in a polluted land”, which is what we are doing right now. It fell first on the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us.

sense.text: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Shiloh, in Ephraim's land, was the first place; look what became of it.
Now the Lord turns to Judah: “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”. They refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust”, “as I have done to Shiloh.” What he did to Ephraim he would do to Judah: let the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. “And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.”

The exact same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

“Beerah his son, whom Tilgath–pilneser king of Assyria carried away captive: he was prince of the Reubenites.” Tiglath-pileser, Pul for short, was the first Assyrian king to go in and conquer the northern kingdom.

It was not done all at once. It was done in waves: he would come in and take out this group, some of Reuben here, some of Asher there, and then his son came along and did the most.

“And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.” So “the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath–pilneser king of Assyria”, the same king, Pul being the short name, “and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day”, unto the day Chronicles was written.

“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord”. Ahaz over Judah, Hoshea over Ephraim.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”. This is Pul's son: Pul is Tiglath-pileser the third, and this is Shalmaneser the fifth. Hoshea became his servant, then turned against him: “he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria”. He tried to align himself with Egypt to defy Assyria, and was shut up in prison.

Assyria besieged Samaria three years, “and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.” That is modern-day Iran, bordering Russia.

The northern kingdom migrated on from there and became the Scythians. We went from Iran over into Russia; some went as far as China, and some as far as Japan and became samurai over there. We kept migrating further and further east. On the map of the fall of Samaria, Gozan, Halah and the river Habor are where the northern kingdom was placed: modern-day Iran, with Russia and China right next door. Ephraim fled into all those areas; the Silk Road, that was us too.
“For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt”, “and had feared other gods”.

“And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God”. They thought God was not watching. God said, I see what you are doing, and I'm going to enslave all of you. They built high places in all their cities.
“And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made with their fathers”, “and they followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen that were round about them”.

“Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.” The southern kingdom was left over, for now.

“Also Judah kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made. And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”. Now God is angry with all twelve: the northern kingdom goes into captivity, and Judah is going next.
“And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”.

The Lord sent lions among the heathen in our land, because they were doing a lot of evil. So the king of Assyria said, carry back one of the priests to “teach them the manner of the God of the land”, so they could sacrifice and stay. “Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth–el, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.” One of Jeroboam's priests was brought back to teach them to sacrifice, to remain in the land in Ephraim's absence.

“Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. They were still allowed their own gods, because the land was defiled already. The northern kingdom was called Samaritans, Samaria being their capital, and these heathen sacrificed in the same high places Ephraim made for their idols: “the men of Babylon made Succoth–benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima”.

So the northern kingdom was carried out of the land, though not all of them: it was done in waves.

“Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it”. Ephraim conspired with the Syrians to overthrow Judah: what the map calls the Syro-Ephraimite war, in the days when wicked, stupid Ahaz was king of Judah.

“Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.” Ahaz was weak and wicked, scared of that alliance.

The Lord sent Isaiah and his son Shear–jashub to meet Ahaz: “Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.” Rezin the Syrian king and Pekah king of Ephraim, joined together.

Their evil counsel: “Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeal”. Take Judah's land and set their own king over it.
“Thus saith the Lord God, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.” That counsel between Syria and Ephraim was not going to happen.

“For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin”: Damascus is Syria's capital and Rezin its ruler. “And within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

This is very important for the whole class. Ephraim shall be broken, “that it be not a people”. It is worded that way for a reason.

precepts.why:
Isaiah wrote “concerning Maher–shalal–hash–baz”, and his son was born and named so: “For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.” By the time the child is of age those kings would be removed. Isaiah's sons were born as signs that Ephraim and Syria would be overthrown by Assyria and never succeed against Judah.

“Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah that go softly”, “the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria”. Assyria would conquer Ephraim and pass through Judah too, “he shall reach even to the neck”, but not take Judah fully like Ephraim. “O Immanuel”: God with us.

“Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces”: Ephraim and Syria shall be broken, Ephraim particularly, not a people. “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought”, “for God is with us.” So do not be afraid of the confederacy, “neither fear ye their fear”, do not be cowardly and weak like Ahaz. “Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.”

“And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel”. Both: it should be one house, but the Lord speaks of Israel as two houses, the house of Judah and the house of Ephraim. The stone is Christ. He is “for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem”, a trap to both houses but specifically to Jerusalem.

“And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken” by that stone of stumbling, that rock of offence. So not only did Ephraim fall physically and spiritually; Judah fell physically and spiritually too, but worse.

sense.text:
“Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” Lo-ruhamah means no mercy, for the house of Israel, the northern kingdom. “Utterly take them away” is Assyria overthrowing Ephraim, that it be not a people.

The children are for signs, named after events that would come upon the nation. Isaiah's sons were a sign that God would spare Judah; Hosea's children were a sign that he would not spare Ephraim.

On the map, Syria with Damascus its capital lies to the north; then Dor, Samaria, Mount Ebal and Gerizim, all the land of Israel, the northern kingdom, because it lies to the north. Judah lies to the south, the southern kingdom: Jerusalem, Hebron and Bethlehem, where David was anointed. Remember the place Dor; it belongs to the northern kingdom.

“But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.” Assyria came up against Judah too but was not successful as it was against Ephraim, because God was with them. We find out how they were saved without going to war in Hezekiah's day.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Lo-ammi means not my people. When you are not God's people and he is not your God, what does that make you? A Gentile. A heathen, a stranger, a non-Israelite. The Lord told Israel through Hosea, you are not my people, I'm not your God, I want nothing to do with you.

Judah read this and said, good. The hell with Ephraim, they are not his people anymore; they are Gentiles, and we don't deal with them.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea”, “and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” Where they were told they were Gentiles, they would be told, no, you are not Gentiles, you are God's people. But Judah forgot this verse.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”: reunited, under one head, Christ. “For great shall be the day of Jezreel”: delivered together, united as one. Judah said, nah, those guys are Gentiles forever. Hosea said, eventually you have to come together again.

precepts.why:
“Thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”: we became Israelites. “Be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”.

Stop: how many nations did Jacob have? One. Jacob gave birth to one nation of people, yet he says a nation and a company of nations. Who could that be? We just read in Hosea that Ephraim would be broken, not a people: a heathen, a Gentile, a nation. Hold that; it comes back with Cornelius.

Moses said the same thing. “He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.” This Rock is the stone of stumbling and rock of offence of Isaiah 8, and he is called our God. Without iniquity: that is Christ, clear cut. Jake says Christ ain't our God: every idle word.

“Their spot is not the spot of his children: they are a perverse and crooked generation. Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?” The foolish people are Israel as a whole. The Rock of verse 4 is our father: he made us, he bought us, purchased and redeemed us, and established us. That is Christ.

“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”: we got rich, rebellious and complacent, “then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods”. “Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful”. So he said, “I will hide my face from them”.

“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people”. The them is the southern kingdom, and those which are not a people is the northern kingdom. Moses was telling you there would be a split even before the split took place: the same split as the nation and the company of nations told to Jacob.

Remember, when the split took place the Lord said, do not fight against the northern kingdom, for this thing is from me. So back to Jacob: “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth”. Our seed shall be the majority of people on the planet, a lot of them watered down and many of them going to die, but as the sand of the sea.

“And thou shalt spread abroad to the west”, through migration, forced migration or captivity: the western hemisphere. “And to the east”: Africa, China, the Pacific Islands, Japan. “And to the north”: Canada, Europe. “And to the south”.

“And in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” The families of the earth are us, scattered into all four corners of the earth: it speaks of Israel, not other nations getting blessed. They get blessed with servitude: spared, not nuked, perpetual employment. No 401k, no retirement plan.

“And they shall hear Jezreel”: Jezreel is Israel. “And I will sow her unto me in the earth”: he adopts Israel back unto him. “And I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy”: that is Israel, Lo-ruhamah.

“And I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.” We're not Gentiles no more; not heathens anymore. Judah said we ain't reading that part, took the black highlighter and covered it, because they were evil and stupid.

sense.text: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded, and he went to meet Asa: “The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.” Asa reigned from 911 to 870 BC.
“Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.” This is talking about the northern kingdom. Hold that.
“But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.”

“And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.”

Whenever Judah was on point, Ephraim would follow along. Every time Judah was on point, whether for the long run or only for a season (Asa went off a little later on), Ephraim would realise the Lord was with him. The Lord always used Judah to bring Ephraim back in. Assyria took them in waves, not all of them, and remnants of Ephraim remained in the land, and Asa reached out to them.

Who are called “the strangers”? Ephraim, the northern kingdom: not my people, not a people. Strangers without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law, because they stopped going to Jerusalem to worship and went to the idols Jeroboam set up in Dan and Bethel. That is very important to remember: the strangers.

precepts.why:
The next good king of Judah, Jehoshaphat, who reigned from 870 to 848 BC, set judges in the fenced cities: “Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord”, “for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” A righteous king.

“And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer–sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.” From Beersheba, where Simeon was, to mount Ephraim: Jehoshaphat caused some of Ephraim to return to the Lord. When Judah was on point, Ephraim followed along; when Judah went off, Ephraim went even worse.

“The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul”, and “they dwelt at Beer–sheba”. Beersheba was Simeon's allotment of land, so from Beersheba is from Simeon: Simeon too came back with the strangers when Judah was on point.

sense.text: Listen carefully to the waves. Pul, Tiglath-pileser, began it around 732 BC. His son Shalmaneser the fifth delivered the final blow around 722 and 721 BC, taking most of Ephraim out of the land. Then came a man named Sargon: “In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it”.

Isaiah walked “naked and barefoot three years for a sign and wonder upon Egypt and upon Ethiopia; So shall the king of Assyria lead away the Egyptians prisoners, and the Ethiopians captives, young and old, naked and barefoot, even with their buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.”

Israel would try to run to both of those places, but Assyria would conquer them both. Sargon conquered the northern kingdom as well, around the same time, 722 and 721 BC.

Hezekiah reigned from about 716 to 686 BC. “And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel.”

Of everything read so far, this is the most important for the main character of this class, Cornelius. Keep it in mind, and remember the place called Dor. Hezekiah wanted Judah and Ephraim to keep the Passover together.
They kept it “in the second month. For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently”. They had messed up the purification the first time.

A decree went out “throughout all Israel, from Beer–sheba even to Dan”: from Simeon at Beersheba all the way to Dan, “for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.” They had been in idolatry.

“Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.” This is after Tiglath-pileser and after Shalmaneser: remnants of Israel escaped and remained in the land, alongside the heathen put there in their place.

And according to Hosea they were all considered Gentiles. Judah said, those are all Gentiles in that area: the Israel that's there are Gentiles, and the heathen put in their place are Gentiles too.
“And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see.”

The posts passed with the letters from city to city “through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun: but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them.” This dude is crazy, keep Passover? We don't deal with y'all, we want no parts of Judah.

“Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.” Not all of them mocked; some took it seriously. When Judah is on point, Ephraim comes along every time. It is going to be the same thing today: all the tribes celebrating Passover.

“Also in Judah the hand of God was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of the Lord.” The Lord was going to use Judah to give all twelve one mind to keep the laws of God. That is why Judah is so important among the tribes.

“Then they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the second month: and the priests and the Levites were ashamed, and sanctified themselves”. Ashamed because they messed up the first month; this time they got it right.

“For there were many in the congregation that were not sanctified”: not purified, meaning unclean. “Therefore the Levites had the charge of the killing of the passovers for every one that was not clean, to sanctify them unto the Lord.”

“For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves”. They showed up, and they were unclean. Keep that in mind: Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, unclean, for the Passover.

“Yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one”. They were able to eat the Passover anyway while unclean, because Judah prayed for them.
“That prepareth his heart to seek God, the Lord God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary.” Though he be unclean.
“And the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.” He made them clean. That sounds very familiar: it sounds very much like the New Testament.

precepts.why:
This is why the hand of God was in Judah. “Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father’s children shall bow down before thee. Judah is a lion’s whelp”.

“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: that is kingship. “Nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: the lawgivers, the priests, are in Judah too. Let it sit and sizzle. Judah first.

“Until Shiloh come”: until the king, Christ out of that tribe, comes. “And unto him shall the gathering of the people be”: unto Christ of Judah. But he would use his tribe to do it, the way he used Hezekiah to gather Ephraim to the Passover.

sense.text: “Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and entered into Judah, and encamped against the fenced cities, and thought to win them for himself”, purposed to fight against Jerusalem. Remember Hosea 1: Judah would not be saved by bow nor by sword, but by the Lord. This is it right here.

Hezekiah stopped the waters of the fountains without the city, “saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?” Don't let them drink our water. He built up the broken wall, “repaired Millo in the city of David, and made darts and shields in abundance.”

He gathered the people and spoke comfortably to them: “Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria”, “for there be more with us than with him”, the angels. “With him is an arm of flesh”: he is just a man. “But with us is the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles.” God with us, Immanuel. He brought them wise words to comfort them.

Sennacherib wrote letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel: “As the gods of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people out of mine hand, so shall not the God of Hezekiah deliver his people out of mine hand.” Your God is not going to help you either. They cried in the Jews' speech to the people on the wall “to affright them”, to scare them, and spoke against the God of Jerusalem as against gods made with hands.

Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah prayed and cried to heaven, “And the Lord sent an angel, which cut off all the mighty men of valour, and the leaders and captains in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land.” The angel came through and killed the army outside the land, and his own sons slew him with the sword.

precepts.why:
How many did the angel kill? “Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand”: one angel killed 185,000 of his men. “And when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead”: he killed them in their sleep.

“So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” As he worshipped in the house of Nisroch his god, “Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esar–haddon his son reigned in his stead.” He lost 185,000 men in their sleep and went home angry. What did he do with that anger? Tobit tells us.

Tobit, “of the tribe of Nephthali; Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe”, “which is called properly Nephthali in Galilee above Aser”. Enemessar is the Greek form of Shalmaneser, Shalmaneser the fifth, the same king. “I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve”. He was taken captive.

“The most High gave me grace and favour before Enemessar, so that I was his purveyor”: he oversaw the food and rations. Then “when Enemessar was dead, Sennacherib his son reigned in his stead”. Sennacherib is the one who attacked Hezekiah and lost the 185,000.

Tobit “gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” Assyria was very brutal and vicious: they would take Israelites to the top of the walls and throw them off, and if he found his brethren broken on the ground, he buried them.

“And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many”. Why did he flee from Judea? Because he lost 185,000 men. He was mad he could not overthrow Judah, so out of anger he started killing Ephraim.

Tobit was reported and his goods “were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Within fifty-five days Sennacherib's sons killed him, “and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead; who appointed over his father’s accounts, and over all his affairs, Achiacharus my brother Anael’s son.” His nephew became the king's accountant, and Tobit gained status through him. Remember Tobit's alms.

sense.text:
Josiah reigned from 640 to 609 BC. The money for the house of God was gathered “of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin”. Manasseh and Ephraim donated toward the temple in Jerusalem.

Why “the remnant”? Because Assyria had taken most of them out of the land; remnants remained, some idolatrous and some faithful. Again, whenever Judah is on point, Ephraim follows along.

“When at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun”: the same Zebulun that came and kept the Passover under Hezekiah. “And the land of Naphtali”: Tobit was of Naphtali. They were afflicted, “and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Galilee of the Gentiles, where the northern kingdom lived. They were called Gentiles.

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”. The people are the people of verse 1, Naphtali and Zebulun, the northern kingdom: those in darkness saw a great light in Galilee. “They that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.”

“For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor”. “But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire”: that is the war coming now in our time, nuclear war.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, not unto all. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God”. Y'all say Christ ain't God: he is not the Father, but he is God.

“The everlasting Father”: because he is our maker, the Rock that begat thee in Deuteronomy 32. That is why he is called our father. “The Prince of Peace”: he must bring peace between those who have a hatred for each other, who are divided among themselves. That is why he is the Prince of Peace.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David”. Peace means there will be no more division or hatred between the two kingdoms. Who is this talking about? Christ.

“The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” The word in verse 8 is the same as the son given and the child born in verse 6: the word of God. And it lighted upon Israel, the light that shined on those in darkness in verse 2. It is not upon all nations.

“And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. They shall know regarding that son that is born, that word sent into Jacob. Ephraim and Samaria: Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern kingdom, shall know him.

“That say in the pride and stoutness of heart, The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars.” We'll have our own place of worship, Gerizim, Shiloh. The Lord says no, you have to go to Judah. It is not going to happen.

This is the time of Persia. We went from Assyria, then Babylon conquered Judah, and now we are in the Persian captivity. “When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”.

They came to Zerubbabel and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”. Let us join, let us learn together, a rainbow coalition, let's integrate: we know you're the real Jews, we want to follow your God. It is the same as the Japanese man in the Black Panthers shown at the start of the class: he joined at the very beginning, rose in the ranks to field marshal, and all along was an FBI informant for fifteen years. When you allow yourself to become weak and let your emotions grant heathens access, that is what they do.

“And we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.” Esar-haddon, Sennacherib's son, brought more heathens into the land of Ephraim, because Ephraim had a lot of land. They had to sacrifice to our God to stay there or the lions would kill them. So, we know about your God, let us join your movement and get salvation too. That sounds like Christianity now: we're all one, neither Jew nor Greek.

“But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Israel, said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel”. They would not allow them in, because they knew they would infiltrate. They were not sincere, just like that informant. Israel understood these nations cannot be trusted among us: they come in, rise in the ranks, take over and destroy from the inside.

Be very mindful, Israel: they try to use Cornelius as a way to grant the nations salvation. That is infiltration. When you start hearing that the nations can be saved and join in, money is involved, the alphabet agencies are involved. Either you're working for Satan or you're working for Satan: the spiritual demon or his children, and both are called Satan. Our forefathers are reminding us the nations are still the same: they lie, they want to be part of the mission, they offer money and fame.

When Israelites start using words like exegesis and eisegesis and hermeneutics, running into the Greek and Latin, that is a fearful spirit taking up Esau's talking points: we can't beat these guys, let's adapt. No. The Bible is fine, the precepts are good. That is Jesuit, Christian missionary stuff, Satan's militia, the same people who killed the Native Americans, the caciques and the Taínos. Hermeneutics has Hermes in it, the trickster god of interpretations. They put out revised Bibles after the sixties that twist the words: take the word black out and put mourning, take a whole verse out because they know what it means. Very dark is not the same as black: a dark car could be any colour; a black car is black.

Whatever we say the Bible says, that's what it means. That is not pride, it is confidence. That is our book. We don't need Esau to give us back our own book.

“When they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their’s, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground”. “But now are they returned to their God, and are come up from the places where they were scattered, and have possessed Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is”.

So Judith takes place in the time of Persia, when they returned from exile and the sanctuary was built. Not Babylon: the Persian captivity. That is the time frame of Judith.

Now the Greeks. “Wherefore we have ratified unto them the borders of Judea, with the three governments of Apherema and Lydda and Ramathem, that are added unto Judea from the country of Samaria”. The Greeks had all of Israel to themselves, and as a kind of alliance they rewarded the southern kingdom, the Hasmonean family of Levi, with portions of the land of Samaria, the northern kingdom. The lands, not the people.

“I confirm thee in the high priesthood, and appoint thee ruler over the four governments”. Portions of the northern kingdom were given back, and that gave the remnants of the northern kingdom who had been exiled the opportunity to return to their allotments during the time of the Greeks. Judah moved into those lands too: Christ was in Galilee, the northern kingdom's land.
Now Rome. Remember Isaiah 9: even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria shall know. Christ “left Judea, and departed again into Galilee. And he must needs go through Samaria.”

“Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob bought that ground for Joseph, and it went to Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh. On the map Sychar sits right by Ebal and Gerizim. “Now Jacob’s well was there.”

“Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The Samaritans were the northern kingdom. The Jews had no dealings with them: the same beef read about all class.

Christ offered her living water. “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? Who does she call our father? Jacob, the father of the Israelites. So she was Israel. Which child of Jacob got the well? Joseph: Ephraim got the well. She knew, but she said we don't deal with each other, from that beef way back.

Some people say she was lying, as if she had some kind of power so Christ couldn't see what she was. You can't make this up.

“Sir, give me this water”. “Go, call thy husband, and come hither.” “I have no husband.” “Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.” The man she was with was not her husband: she was up there fornicating, whoring.

What does that prove? That just because you stick your rod in a woman, that does not make her your wife. Sex by itself does not constitute marriage. Negroes run around poking sisters and saying you my wife. That's a heavy point. He was just banging her; he never took her to be his wife.

She asked for the water, and Christ hit her with the law about fornication. And Christ knew she had five husbands, but couldn't tell what her tribe was? Every idle word.

“Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.” You've got to be a prophet to know that about me. “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: our fathers, Christ's fathers too. Mount Gerizim and Ebal, where all Israel went before Jerusalem, and they still worshipped there. “And ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship”, because that's the place the Lord chose when he refused Ephraim in the Psalms.
“The hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Because Rome would come and destroy them both, Judah and Samaria.
“Ye worship ye know not what”: you don't know what you're doing. “We know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” Salvation comes from Judah: you've got to listen to Judah first and foremost.

“The woman saith unto him, I know”. Remember Isaiah 9: they shall know. “I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.” She knew the prophecy, that those of Samaria would know when Christ was coming.

“I that speak unto thee am he.” His disciples came “and marvelled that he talked with the woman”. Why marvel? Because the Jews did not deal with the Samaritans; they themselves did not talk to the northern kingdom: why are you talking to her, we don't deal with those people. But those are our people. “Yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why talkest thou with her?” They would not dare ask Christ that.
“Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?” Is not this the Messiah?

“So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days”, teaching them. “Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.” And know. The world is Israel: us. After two days he went back home into Galilee.

precepts.why: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Hosea said leave them alone, and Judah took that as: the hell with them, they're cast off. They forgot the part that said they would be gathered together and appoint themselves one head. That was dismissed, because of the hatred they had for each other. That is why the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans.

Read it again so you don't lose the thought: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. Shall know. And the woman of Samaria says, I know that Messias cometh. The prophecy fulfilled at the well.

sense.text:
The man of the hour. “There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band”. Where is Cornelius from? Not Italy: Caesarea.

On the maps, Dor sits in Samaria, and right under it is Strato's Tower, which is Caesarea Maritima. There are three Caesareas: one in Africa, not written of; Caesarea Philippi; and Caesarea Maritima, where Cornelius is from. When Rome colonized our land they named it after Caesar, Caesarea Maritima, because it is a port on the water. It is the land of West Manasseh: Manasseh dwelt on both sides of Jordan, east and west, and this was Manasseh's allotment right under Ephraim. Joseph's sons. The same region where Christ spoke to the woman at the well. Asher shared that port, of course, but it was Manasseh's land.

He was of the Italian band, the Roman army, not Italian. There were Israelites in Rome's military like there are Israelites in America's military. Negroes love master so much they see the word Italian and get excited: yes, he's white, I knew it. No. You big dummy. A centurion was over a hundred men.

“A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” That is the exact same thing Tobit of Naphtali said he did: he gave alms always.

He saw an angel of God in a vision about the ninth hour: “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God. And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side”. Peter lived in Joppa and would sail thirty to forty miles up the coast to Caesarea Maritima, just below Dor. Cornelius sent two household servants and a devout soldier.

Peter went up on the housetop to pray, grew hungry, and fell into a trance, “And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. Knit at the four corners: remember the Lord told Jacob his children would spread abroad to the west, the east, the north and the south. In it were “all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.”

“Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” “But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” Remember the feast held by a particular king, and the particular people who came to keep it, and were not clean.

“What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” This is not talking about no damn animals; this ain't talking about pork. “This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.” The vessel knit at the four corners went back up.

“Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean”: he was thinking the same thing Christians think, that he was being told to eat unclean food, which the law forbids. Then the men from Cornelius stood at the gate, “the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.” Three times the vision, and three men at the door: now he starts to put it together. “Go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.”

“Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews”. He sought God; and God had said through Hezekiah, pardon every one that prepareth his heart to seek him.

Peter went with certain brethren from Joppa, and Cornelius had called together “his kinsmen and near friends.” Cornelius fell at his feet and worshipped him, “But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.”

“Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. Sound familiar? The same thing the woman told Christ at the well: the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.

“But God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man. Not food, not animals: any man. So the vision was about a man, Cornelius.

One of another nation: remember Jacob was told a nation and a company of nations would come of him. Cornelius was of another nation, the other kingdom, the northern kingdom. Who did Judah call common and unclean? The northern kingdom: not my people, not their God, strangers.

Cornelius rehearses what happened before Peter came: fasting four days, praying at the ninth hour, a man in bright clothing said, “Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.”

“Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” In every nation, because Israel is scattered into every nation.
They always skip verse 36. “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”: the word was sent to the children of Israel. “Preaching peace by Jesus Christ”, because he is the Prince of Peace.

“That word, I say, ye know”. Ye know: Isaiah 9 said those of Samaria shall know, and the woman at the well said I know. Cornelius was devout and knew the law; he knew the word that “began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached”.

“God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power”, “for God was with him.” Immanuel. “Whom they slew and hanged on a tree”: they lynched him on a cross. “Him God raised up the third day”, shown “unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead.”

He is “the Judge of quick and dead”, the living and the dead. “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” Isn't that what Cornelius is receiving?

precepts.why:
Some will say that's just a map, it ain't in the Bible. So here it is in the scriptures, for the doubters. “And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem”. Tappuah on Manasseh's border belonged to Ephraim, and “Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border”: the Mediterranean is his border, the coast Peter sailed up from Joppa.

“They met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east. And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth–shean and her towns”, “and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns”. Dor, and under it Caesarea Maritima: all that was Dor's towns before. Endor, Taanach, Megiddo. “Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities”: there were too many of them.

That is Manasseh's land, and that is where Cornelius lived: Caesarea, in the land of West Manasseh.

“Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” That is the vessel knit at the four corners.

A vessel wherein is no pleasure means unclean: it is no good, it cannot be used. Vessels are used in the temple for service, but a vessel of no pleasure cannot be used for temple service; it is deemed unclean. Israel among the Gentiles is that vessel.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations”: the nations is Israel. “And shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah, as Hosea said, from the four corners: a vessel knit at the four corners.

Go back to Hezekiah's Passover: “For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh”, and Caesarea is Manasseh's land, “Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves”. They were unclean.

“But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one That prepareth his heart to seek God, the Lord God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed”. In other words, I will not call them unclean. Did Cornelius prepare his heart to seek God? Was he a devout man who gave alms? Yes, he was.

“And the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.” He made them clean. That is what God hath cleansed: call not thou common.

“And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all”: Judah and Ephraim gathered together. “And they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. Two nations, Judah and Israel: both the houses of Isaiah 8.

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols”, “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them”. Make them clean: both kingdoms. “So shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” So when Peter speaks of “one of another nation”, the other nation is the other kingdom.

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Israel is scattered everywhere, into all four corners, the vessel knit at the four corners. So “in every nation” he that feareth him is Israel found in every nation.

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered”: that word whosoever again. “For in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance”: in Mount Zion and Jerusalem, not everywhere in all the heathen nations. “And in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” That's it.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”. “To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins”. Unto his people, the remission of their sins.

So the word brought to Cornelius, the remission of sins, was brought unto his people. That includes Cornelius.

sense.text: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” Simeon is Simon Peter, and the first visit to the Gentiles is Peter going to Cornelius.
“And to this agree the words of the prophets”: prophets, more than one.

“After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. When David reigned, he reigned over all twelve tribes: the tabernacle of David is all twelve under their king. In Peter's time were the twelve tribes reunited? No, still fallen.

“And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”: reunite all twelve. That is what Ezekiel said, no more two nations but one; and Hosea, Judah and Ephraim gathered together under one head.

“That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”. What has to happen first, before men seek after the Lord? The tribes come together first. So what was happening in Acts 10, verse 16 or verse 17? Verse 16 happens first: the rebuilding of the tabernacle of David.

precepts.why:
It is written a bit differently in the New Testament, for reasons not explained here, but it is the same thing. “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”: all twelve tribes, fallen in Peter's time. “And close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”: those who will seek after God at that time. In Acts 10, is verse 11 taking place or verse 12? Verse 11. Verse 11 must take place for verse 12 to happen. Who was part of that tabernacle of David being raised? Peter, and Cornelius.

Even today, what are we doing? We are rebuilding the tabernacle of David that is fallen, standing back upon our feet. But Amos speaks of when it will be fully established: when Christ returns and rebuilds us as in the days of old. Then the nations will seek after the Lord, because we are going to force them.

sense.text: Acts 11 gives an elaborate explanation of what took place in chapter 10 with Cornelius, like a replay. “The apostles and brethren that were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God”: Cornelius and his household.
“They that were of the circumcision contended with him”: Judah. “Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” You went to heathens and sat and ate with them.
“But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them”: he explains Acts 10.

Before Peter went to Cornelius, who were they teaching? “They which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” The Ethiopian in Acts 8 was a Jew. Everything before Cornelius was taught to the Jews.

“That he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”, “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles”. Not of Judah only: the called are Jews and Gentiles.

“As he saith also in Osee”: the prophets agree. “I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.” Who is that talking about? The northern kingdom: that's Hosea 1. “In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.”

So the Jews and the Gentiles are explained in Hosea 1:10-11. The Jews are Judah. Then who are the Gentiles? The northern kingdom. See how easy that is.

Someone says, no, this is a comparison, not actual Israel. Read the next verse: “Esaias also crieth concerning Israel”. Also concerning Israel: so Hosea was talking about Israel too. “Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved”. Some of y'all work for Satan or work for Satan.

“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. Remember Isaiah 7 and Deuteronomy 32: not a people. These strangers are the same strangers of Ephraim and Manasseh who came to Judah when Judah was on point, the strangers who came up to Jerusalem in Chronicles.

“Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. The strangers of verse 1 are the elect. Who is that? Israel. The Jews and Gentiles of Romans 9 were called according to Hosea and according to Isaiah: these strangers are Israel. “Through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ”.

precepts.why:
“But unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed”: the disobedient were the southern kingdom, the Pharisees who rejected him; the builders are the disobedient who rejected Christ and went against that stone of stumbling of Isaiah 8. “The same is made the head of the corner”: that same Rock that made us became our elder, our leader, the high priest.

“And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence”: Isaiah 8:14, said right here. “Even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient”: the Pharisees, the southern kingdom. “Whereunto also they were appointed.” Appointed to put Christ to death; and Christ's death granted the other kingdom the chance to repent and come back into the fold. By rejecting Christ they ended up bringing their brothers back in. They were blinded so that the northern kingdom could return.

“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”: the ye is the same strangers Peter wrote to in chapter 1, the elect. “Who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”: that's Isaiah 9, the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.

“Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”: back to Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 7 and 8, not a people. “Which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi: no mercy, not my people, and now the people of God. That is who Cornelius was.
